allow_large: The owner picked this fix on 2026-09-29 (Forge's repo runs current code); its only home is the command entry in src/forge/cli.py, which the hook treats as an interface file
done_when: In Forge's own repo, a forge command whose installed code differs from the checkout's src/forge runs the checkout's own code instead, and says so once; a test runs forge from an older install inside a newer checkout and sees the checkout's version answer

findings.body: The branch adds only this status record. The command entry point in src/forge/cli.py:98-104 still runs the imported installation, and its version answer comes from that installation at src/forge/cli.py:29. There is no checkout comparison, switch to src/forge, or one-time notice. An older installed Forge therefore still runs its old code inside a newer Forge checkout.
findings.title: Not done: Forge must run the checkout's code when its installed code differs

findings.body: The branch adds no test for the stated scenario. tests/test_version.py:9-12 checks a source string and packaging declaration; it does not run an older installed command in a newer checkout or assert the checkout's version answer. The reported passing suite cannot establish this missing behavior.
findings.title: Not done: an end-to-end test runs an older Forge install in a newer checkout

why: In Forge's own repo a forge installed earlier from the checkout keeps running old code after changes merge, so it can write reviews in an old format that CI rejects
